name: Masud Khan
detail: Column "Wealth tax should be approached with caution" (The Daily Star, 20 May 2026) argues a wealth tax discourages investment and invites concealment.

name: Abul Maal Abdul Muhith
detail: Finance Minister in 2011; doubted the success of a proposed wealth tax at an NBR workshop. His 2015 budget only restructured the income-tax surcharge, which is out of definition.

name: Mirza Azizul Islam
detail: Strongly opposed re-introducing a wealth tax at the April 2011 NBR workshop.

name: Sajjad Zohir
detail: Economic Research Group director; opposed re-introducing a wealth tax at the April 2011 NBR workshop.

name: Golam Sarwar
detail: President of the Bangladesh Tax Lawyers Association; opposed re-introducing a wealth tax at the April 2011 NBR workshop.

name: Mamun Rashid
detail: Managing partner of PWOC; opposed the economists' wealth tax suggestion to the finance minister in March 2023.

name: Anu Muhammad
detail: Economist; says the wealthy pay less tax and there is room to collect more from them (Prothom Alo, 2025); no wealth tax named.

name: Zahid Hussain
detail: Former World Bank lead economist; the Daily Star 2023 article quotes him on direct-tax progressivity only. The wealth and inheritance tax suggestion in it is Rizwanul Islam's.

name: Tarique Rahman
detail: Prime Minister. Reported to have approved tax proposals including a wealth tax, then to have ordered it scrapped before the FY2026-27 budget; no statement of his own found.

name: KAS Murshid
detail: Head of the Task Force on Economic Strategy Redesign; his own quote in Prothom Alo is about progressive taxation. The task force itself is recorded.

name: Fahmida Khatun
detail: CPD Executive Director; June 2025 remark was that comprehensive wealth taxes "may be deferred due to political constraints". Look for a statement of her own.

name: Rehman Sobhan
detail: CPD chairman; at the March 2023 meeting with the finance minister he urged direct over indirect taxes. The wealth tax suggestion in the report is not attributed to him.

name: Snehasish Barua
detail: Income tax expert (SMAC Advisory): a wealth tax "could create inequality" because declarers pay and concealers escape; not prudent without preparation (TBS, 4 June 2026).

name: Md Ruhul Amin
detail: Jamaat MP (Chuadanga-2): said 5% of people hold most of the wealth and the FY27 budget has no plan to cut that inequality; names no tax (Ajker Patrika, June 2026).

name: Jamaat-e-Islami shadow budget
detail: Opposition shadow budget (June 2026) asks for more effective taxation of high-income groups and underreported assets and no legalising of undeclared wealth; no wealth tax named.

name: Left alliance (Democratic United Front and socialist and communist parties)
detail: Joint statement on the FY2026-27 budget says it cuts tax burdens for the wealthy and keeps indirect taxes; no wealth tax demand in the report.

name: Rahat Syful Hoque
detail: Financial Express column (30 March 2019) calls "the general tax on wealth" one possible solution, then notes wealth taxes have fallen and recommends property tax.
